citation.journal: Journal of the Royal Army Medical Corps

record.population: 311 male British Army soldiers assessed at a cold injury clinic; the paper compares "African Americans", Pacific Islanders and Gurkhas with Caucasians
record.design: Retrospective analysis of peripheral cold weather injury by ethnic origin
record.finding: Those classed as African Americans (the paper's own term, in the British Army; the abstract does not say how ethnicity was assigned) had a relative incidence of cold injury of 30.36 (95% CI 25.82-35.70) against Caucasian soldiers and were more severely affected (mean score 5.39 against 4.24).
record.note: tier_variant observational-black-population. Clinic-attendee data, so the relative incidence is among those attending; the abstract does not give denominators. Small number of cases in the group. Measures cold weather injury at work, not voluntary cold-water immersion.
